prompt: Lívia is asked why October 2025 fell when no other month did. Which kind of analysis is that question?
hint: It asks about the past, and it asks why.

choices.text: Descriptive, because the month is over
choices.why: Descriptive analysis found that October fell. Asking why is the next kind.

choices.text: Diagnostic
choices.why: Right: it works on a finished period and asks for the cause, which is lesson 7.

choices.text: Predictive, since the answer shapes next October
choices.why: Predictive analysis looks at what has not happened yet. October 2025 is over.

choices.text: Prescriptive, because the answer will lead to an action
choices.why: Most answers lead to an action somewhere. Prescriptive analysis is the one that chooses the action; this question chooses nothing.

prompt: None of these questions is in the lesson. Match each to its kind of analysis.
hint: Past or future; counting, explaining, foreseeing or choosing.

pairs.left: Which three products had the most returns in March?
Why did returns of garden chairs double in March?
How many orders will the online shop take on the first Saturday of December?
How many delivery vans should be hired for December?

prompt: The four kinds are often drawn as a staircase. What does the lesson say is wrong with that picture?
hint: What does a forecast extend?

choices.text: The order of the steps: predictive analysis is in fact harder than prescriptive analysis
choices.why: The lesson keeps the order, and says value and difficulty grow along it.

choices.text: It leaves out a fifth kind of analysis that sits between diagnostic and predictive
choices.why: The lesson names four kinds and no fifth.

choices.text: It treats descriptive as a step to leave behind, when the rest stand on it
choices.why: Right: a diagnosis explains a described number, a forecast extends a counted series, and a recommendation is judged by a later description.

choices.text: It makes descriptive analysis look more valuable than it is
choices.why: The staircase puts descriptive on the lowest step, so it makes it look less valuable, not more.

prompt: Put the four kinds in the order the course teaches them, which is also the order each needs the one before.
hint: From what happened to what to do.
items: Predictive: what is likely to happen
Prescriptive: what to do about it
trap: Prescriptive and predictive are the pair people swap: a recommendation needs a forecast first, so predictive comes before it.

prompt: A store sold 980 thousand reais in March 2024 and 1,050 thousand in March 2025. What is the growth year over year, in percent to one decimal?
Why does the lesson prefer comparing a month with the same month a year before, at Varanda?
hint: May has Mother's Day in every year.

choices.text: Because a year-ago number is already audited by the accounts, and last month's is not yet
choices.why: Auditing is not the lesson's reason; the calendar is.

choices.text: Because the months are not alike, and the same month a year before has the same season
choices.why: Right: comparing with last month mostly measures the season, and the season repeats every year.

choices.text: Because it gives bigger percentages
choices.why: It gives smaller ones at Varanda: 3.9 to 8.4 against swings of 26.1 and −16.8. Size is not the point either way.

choices.text: Because month-over-month growth is computed with the wrong formula
choices.why: Both use the same formula, new over old minus one. They differ in which old value they use.

prompt: Renata's team celebrates: November 2025 sold 26.1% more than October 2025. What does that number tell you about how November went?
hint: What did November 2024 do against October 2024?

choices.text: That November grew faster than any other month of 2025, whatever it is compared with
choices.why: It is the biggest month-over-month swing, and that swing is mostly the season. Year over year, December grew more.

choices.text: Little on its own: the same rise shows up every year, with the season
choices.why: Right: November 2024 was up 16.1% on October 2024. The comparison that says how November went is with November 2024: 7.8%.

choices.text: That October was a bad month, which the 26.1% proves
choices.why: October's fall shows year over year (−0.7%). A month-over-month rise does not prove anything about the month before it.

choices.text: That the online campaign worked better than last year's did
choices.why: Nothing in a total says which channel or campaign moved it; that is a diagnosis, and it needs more than one number.

prompt: In your sheet, what share of Varanda's 2024 sales was December, in percent to one decimal?
hint: December 2024 is B13 and the 2024 total is B14.

prompt: Comparing a month with the same month a year before removes the ___, which repeats every year and would otherwise swamp the year's own story.
hint: Mother's Day, the gift months.

prompt: A store grows 10% one year and 10% the next. How much bigger is it after the two years, in percent to one decimal?
hint: Each year's growth is on a base the year before already raised.

prompt: The average of the twelve year-over-year rates is 5.6, and the year grew 5.7. Why do they differ?
hint: How many votes does February get in each?

choices.text: Rounding: each monthly rate was rounded to one decimal place before the average was taken
choices.why: Rounding moves the average by hundredths. The gap comes from weighting, and it stays without any rounding.

choices.text: The average left October out because it was negative
choices.why: AVERAGE counts negative numbers like any other.

choices.text: One of them is wrong, and the year's total should be corrected to 5.6
choices.why: Both are correct arithmetic. They answer different questions.

choices.text: The average gives each month one vote; the year weighs each month by its size
choices.why: Right: December is the largest month and grew 8.4%, so it pulls the year up more than the average.

prompt: A category was 4% of a store's sales last year and 6% this year. Which sentence is correct?
hint: A difference of two percentages is in points.

choices.text: Its share rose by 2 percentage points
choices.why: Right: 6 minus 4 is 2 points. As a growth of one share over the other it is 50%, a different number with a different word.

choices.text: Its share rose by 2%
choices.why: 2 is the difference in points. Called a percent, it reads as a growth of 2%, when the share grew by half.

choices.text: Its share rose by 2 percentage points, which is the same as 2%
choices.why: Points and percent are different things here: 2 points, and 50% growth of the share.

choices.text: Its share rose by 33%, because 2 is a third of 6
choices.why: Growth divides by the old value, 4, not the new one. Divided by 4, it is 50%.

prompt: Which of these statements about growth are correct? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two of the four are arithmetic the lesson ran in the sheet.

choices.text: Sales that fall 10% and then rise 10% end 1% below where they started
choices.why: Right: 100 × 0.9 × 1.1 is 99. The rise was on 90.

choices.text: The denominator of a growth rate is the old value
choices.why: Right: new over old, minus one.

choices.text: Three years at 5.7% a year add up to 17.1% in total
choices.why: Growth compounds: the sheet gives 18.1%.

choices.text: The average of the monthly rates is the year's growth rate
choices.why: Only when every month is the same size. At Varanda the two are 5.6 and 5.7.

prompt: October 2025 fell R$ 60 thousand against October 2024. Why does the lesson say a report should give the percentage as well?
hint: A change is a change on something.

choices.text: Because percentages are easier to type into a spreadsheet
choices.why: Typing has nothing to do with it; the base does.

choices.text: Because reais change with inflation and percentages do not
choices.why: Inflation is a real issue across years (lesson 16), but not the reason here.

choices.text: Because 60 thousand reais is too small an amount to report on its own
choices.why: Whether it is small depends on the base, which is exactly what the reais alone do not say.

choices.text: The reader needs the base: 60 thousand is 0.7% of 8,020
choices.why: Right: the same change in reais is a different size on a different base.

prompt: Which of these belong in Lívia's descriptive report for 2025? Choose all that apply.
hint: Five parts, and one thing the report leaves out.

choices.text: An online order counts on the day it was paid
choices.why: Right: that is the definition, the part Varanda learnt the hard way.

choices.text: The ERP's sales table, loaded on 12 January
choices.why: Right: the source, the first thing checked when a number surprises somebody.

choices.text: October probably fell because of the rain
choices.why: An unchecked cause travels with the authority of the count. It goes on the list of questions, not into the report.

choices.text: Against the same months of 2024, counted the same way
choices.why: Right: the comparison, which says whether the number is good.

prompt: Lívia suspected why October fell. Why did she leave the suspicion out of the descriptive report?
hint: Which half of the sentence was counted?

choices.text: The guess would borrow the authority of the count
choices.why: Right: it is a question for diagnostic work, lesson 7, until somebody checks it.

choices.text: Directors at Varanda do not want to read explanations
choices.why: They want them, which is why lesson 7 exists. They do not want a guess dressed as a finding.

choices.text: A report has a word limit
choices.why: Length is not the reason; the suspicion had not been checked.

choices.text: The suspicion was about the weather, and weather data is not part of BI
choices.why: Weather data can be checked like any other. The problem was that nobody had checked it.

prompt: What is the source row of a descriptive report for, according to the lesson?
hint: Otávio and the accounts.

choices.text: To give credit to whoever built the pipeline
choices.why: Credit is not the point. Checking is.

choices.text: To let a reader check a surprising number against where it came from
choices.why: Right: it tells Otávio which figure in the accounts to compare it with, and whether late returns could still move it.

choices.text: To satisfy the tax authority, which requires it
choices.why: An internal sales report is not a tax filing; lesson 21 is about reports somebody outside requires.

choices.text: To show the data came from an expensive and well-known system, which reassures readers
choices.why: The name of the system matters only because it says where to check.

prompt: A good descriptive report ends with the ___: the one sentence somebody will repeat in a meeting, written by the analyst so the reader does not write their own.
hint: The fifth part.

prompt: A store manager writes: "January was great: sales up 12% on December." What should Lívia ask before she believes it?
hint: At Varanda, January is smaller than December every year.

choices.text: Whether the 12% was rounded up from something like 11.5%, which flatters it
choices.why: Half a point of rounding changes nothing here. The comparison is the problem.

choices.text: Whether the figure includes the online shop's sales as well as the store's
choices.why: A store's own sales would not include them, and the definition is not what makes the sentence odd.

choices.text: How it compares with the same month a year before
choices.why: Right: a January above December is itself strange in a seasonal business, and the like-for-like comparison is with last January.

choices.text: Nothing: month over month is the standard comparison
choices.why: It is the comparison people reach for first, and in a seasonal business it mostly measures the calendar.

prompt: Which of these sentences is a descriptive finding in the lesson's sense?
hint: Period, comparison, a number, and no cause nobody checked.

choices.text: Sales are strong and growing, especially in the online shop
choices.why: No period, no comparison, no number: the reader fills all three from memory.

choices.text: October fell 0.7% because the online campaign moved to November
choices.why: The count is descriptive; the "because" is a diagnosis, and it belongs in a diagnostic report once it has been tested.

choices.text: Q4 2025 was 30.9% of the year, the same share as in 2024
choices.why: Right: a period, a number and a comparison, with nothing guessed.

choices.text: We will sell more in 2026 than in 2025
choices.why: That is about the future, which makes it a forecast, and one with no range.

prompt: January 2025 sold 6,890 thousand reais. If January 2026 sells 7,350 thousand, what is its growth year over year, in percent to one decimal?
hint: New over old, minus one, times 100.
